judgement-on-digest-echo: Asked whether echoing a validator-reported canonical digest into reviewed-card-sha256 is a legitimate review record or a way to bypass the check. Reproduced the mechanism in a throwaway copy: `ce task validate` prints 'this card digests to <hex>' and that value, pinned in the receipt, makes the card pass. Two probes show what the pin actually means: the digest covers the entire card including its review-metadata frontmatter (mutating '## Summary' or deleting the quality-review-* block each produce a different digest), and it is not reproducible outside CE (the file's own sha256 differs from the canonical one). So the pin certifies exactly one thing: the card text has not changed since the receipt was written. It is NOT evidence that a review happened — a single round-trip yields a passing value with zero review performed. It is therefore a legitimate review record only when a genuine review produced the receipt, and a bypass when it does not. ISSUE-001's new section states precisely this ('검토 없이 digest만 채우는 것은 여전히 위조다'), so it does not overstate. Two caveats the issue should eventually carry: the canonicalization is CE-internal, so no human or third tool can independently verify the pin; and the check only fires for a done card that declares `blocks:`, so most of the board is never digest-checked at all.

findings.title: ISSUE-009's Evidence miscounts and omits the tightest file in the repository

It then says '그중 상한에서 200바이트 이내가 다섯 장' and lists five; the true count is six. The omitted file is workflows/dva-dogfood/ref-artifacts.md at 10234 bytes — 6 bytes of headroom, tighter than every file the issue names, and unchanged by this branch so it was omitted at measurement time too. tools/doccheck/policy.go:31 puts workflows/ squarely in the size-enforced scope, so it is not out of scope. findings.title: The recorded 6-failure observation is not reproducible in the worktree as committed
findings.detail: The section states that `ce task validate --all` in the TASK-380 worktree raised failures from five to six, with TASK-379 failing because its receipt cannot be read. My run in this worktree reports exactly five failures and TASK-379 as valid. Cause established after the fact: the team lead disclosed that before spawning the reviewer they copied tasks' TASK-379 receipt from the primary checkout into this worktree's gitignored tmp/, precisely because validate had reported six. So the 5->6 observation was true when recorded and is unreproducible now only because its cause was removed. The finding is therefore about the WRITING, not the fact: the passage reads as a standing property of the worktree, and a later reader re-running the command sees five and concludes the record is wrong. Reproduction confirmed by the reviewer against a card copy with no receipt beside it: 'quality-review-receipt tmp/task-management/direct/queue-run/task-379-review-receipt.json cannot be read: ... no such file or directory'.
findings.recommended-fix: State the sequence rather than the state, and give the command that reproduces it from nothing: fresh worktree of this branch -> `ce task validate --all` -> 6 failures -> copy the receipt from the primary checkout -> 5. Do not drop the observation; it is the sharpest evidence ISSUE-001 has that Summary item 3 is a correctness problem and not an inconvenience.
